doc.title: Marian McPartland — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Promising young artists: Benny Green and Geoff Keezer
summary: She names Benny Green, whom she first heard with Art Blakey, and Geoff Keezer as young artists developing well.

bands.name: Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: I want to talk about in addition still along the lines of “Piano Jazz.” We talked about some of the grand masters and maybe some of your contemporaries as well. Who are some of the younger people, younger artists that have made an impression or that you feel that has, maybe we should just single it to . . . I don’t want to limit it to just the pianists or anything. Are there any young artists that come to mind? I mean, if this question was directed to me, I’ll think of someone like Christian McBride or Donald Brown or somebody or whatever. But if they were directed toward you, who, maybe in addition to those names, who would you say that you feel real good about their, the way their career is developing and how they’re developing as an artist?

God . . . I would have to say Benny Green of course. Somebody told me about him when he was with Art [Blakey]. I was in California, and I went to Catalina’s Restaurant, because Art was there, just to hear Benny Green. He looked like a kid. He still looks like a kid. He had a high collar on. He looked like a school boy. I remember thinking . . . In fact I know I went back stage and spoke to Art about him. So that’s one guy that I think is doing well in his career, in that he seems to be making certain steps from Art to other things. He went with Ray Brown. Then he got his own thing. He’s certainly one.
Now I haven’t . . . I would certainly say Geoff Keezer, although I haven’t seen too much of him lately.
He’s playing with Ray Brown now. Brilliant, brilliant talent. I’m partial to him.
Oh, I know. We had . . . Another Wisconsin kid, isn’t he?
Oh. He’s something, something to behold. Yeah. Who else would you . . .
